correctness.rationale: The prism has exactly three neighbors per vertex; the local triple condition therefore characterizes every P3-convex subset. The ten-state table excludes precisely adjacent unequal nonzero columns and enumerates all remaining globally compatible cyclic column words. Each closed walk has one canonical start at labeled column zero, hence exact weight trace. Symbolic computation of det(I-tM) from the actual ten-state matrix produces the claimed quadratic-times-quintic; direct graph-neighborhood enumeration for all n=3..9 and independent polynomial recurrence comparisons to n=20 corroborate it. The complement min-degree-two argument and girth-cycle census rigorously prove the extremal coefficients for all n.

value.rationale: The explicit new 2026 program of counting P3-convex graph sets makes cyclic products a natural extension beyond tree/threshold subclasses. The uniform rational cardinality polynomial simultaneously determines exponentially many valid configurations, every set-size coefficient, and all maximally large proper convex sets for a canonical cubic infinite family. Neither generic dynamic programming nor the bare existence of a transfer representation gives the particular evaluated degree-seven denominator or coefficient consequences. The extremal structural corollary links enumerative and graph-convexity questions.
